headline: SpaceXAI releases Grok 4.5 AI model with twice the token efficiency
summary: New AI model costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. Grok 4.5 is comparable to Anthropic's Opus 4.7 but faster and lower-cost.
details: SpaceXAI has released its latest model, Grok 4.5, characterized as a workhorse for tasks like coding, app-building, office work, research, and writing. The model is said to have 'twice greater token efficiency' than other leading models.

Grok 4.5 costs $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, competitive with other models. For comparison, Opus 4.7 costs $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.
The company claims Grok 4.5 is comparable to Opus 4.7 but faster and lower-cost. Elon Musk described it as an 'Opus-class model' on his social media platform X.

headline_marked: SpaceX launches [[Grok 4.5 AI model]] at half rival cost
headline: SpaceX launches Grok 4.5 AI model at half rival cost
summary: SpaceX releases Grok 4.5, an AI model for coding and autonomous agents, priced at $2 per million input tokens. It undercuts rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI.
details: SpaceX released Grok 4.5, its first artificial intelligence model trained specifically for coding and autonomous agents. The model uses half as many tokens per task as comparable models and costs less than half as much.
Grok 4.5 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. This undercuts the premium tiers of rivals like Anthropic's Claude Opus line and OpenAI's frontier models.

The model is competitively positioned, with SpaceX claiming it is 'roughly comparable to Opus 4.7, but much faster.' Grok 4.5 ranked fourth on Artificial Analysis's GDPval-AA v2 index of real-world agentic knowledge work.

The acquisition of Cursor, a coding startup, for $60 billion provides the data and compute resources behind Grok 4.5. Cursor's AI-first code editor generates high-quality interaction data used in Grok's training.
caption:
Can Grok 4.5 disrupt the AI market with its low cost?

SpaceX released Grok 4.5, its first artificial intelligence model trained specifically for coding and autonomous agents. The model uses half as many tokens per task as comparable models and costs less than half as much.

Grok 4.5 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. This undercuts the premium tiers of rivals like Anthropic's Claude Opus line and OpenAI's frontier models.

The model is competitively positioned, with SpaceX claiming it is 'roughly comparable to Opus 4.7, but much faster.' Grok 4.5 ranked fourth on Artificial Analysis's GDPval-AA v2 index of real-world agentic knowledge work.

The acquisition of Cursor, a coding startup, for $60 billion provides the data and compute resources behind Grok 4.5. Cursor's AI-first code editor generates high-quality interaction data used in Grok's training.
